title: Company-wide policies and processes - Consolidated guide
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:
This consolidated guide describes Redwood Inference company-wide policies and end-to-end processes for access and permissions, change management, data management, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel, and internal templates. The intent is to provide a single reference for employees and managers to follow standard procedures, reduce operational risk, and keep compliance evidence auditable.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and third-party vendors with access to Redwood systems or data.
- Covers corporate systems, cloud infrastructure, product environments, and physical office facilities.
- Operational owners for each section are listed below; teams must adapt local runbooks to these standards and link back to this master policy.

Responsibilities:
- People Ops: policy maintenance, travel & expenses administration, onboarding/offboarding coordination.
- Security & Compliance: access controls, data-classification policy, vendor security reviews.
- Finance: procurement approvals, PO issuance, vendor payments.
- Engineering Managers: review role assignments, approve change requests for their services, ensure config drift remediation.

1) Access & Permissions
Purpose: Ensure least-privilege access, timely revocation, and documented role ownership.
Key controls and processes:
- Identity provider: Redwood uses SSO (Okta) for primary authentication and RBAC integration with IAM systems. All production access requires SSO and MFA (TOTP or hardware key).
- Role definitions: Teams must publish role descriptions in their team wiki (owner, read-only, deploy, admin).
- Onboarding checklist (People Ops + Team Owner):
  1. New-hire request submitted via HRIS with required roles.
  2. Team owner verifies access needs within 48 hours.
  3. Admin adds user to appropriate groups in Okta and cloud IAM.
  4. User verifies MFA and signs Acceptable Use Policy.
- Offboarding procedure (critical timeline):
  1. People Ops triggers offboarding in HRIS.
  2. Automated workflow disables SSO and revokes cloud keys within 1 hour of termination for privileged users, 24 hours for standard users.
  3. Team owner confirms removal from project-specific resources and rotates shared credentials if applicable.
- Privileged access reviews: Quarterly review of all admin-level groups. Teams must attest to membership and provide justification.
- Service accounts and keys:
  - All long-lived keys must be centrally managed in the secrets store (HashiCorp Vault).
  - Keys must be rotated at least every 90 days; audit logs must record who requested rotation.
- Emergency access (break-glass):
  - Temporary elevated access can be granted via an approved emergency workflow (ticket in Jira with executive approver). All emergency grants expire automatically after 8 hours and are reviewed post-event.

2) Change Management
Purpose: Reduce risk of unplanned outages through controlled changes, clear approvals, and rollback plans.
Process summary:
- Change types:
  - Standard change: low-risk, pre-authorized (e.g., routine config updates) — logged with post-deploy verification.
  - Normal change: requires change request, approver review, scheduled change window.
  - Emergency change: immediate fix for an ongoing incident; must be documented and reviewed within 48 hours.
- Change request (CR) workflow (normal changes):
  1. Submit CR in the Change Management Jira project with owner, impact, roll-forward/rollback plan, test plan, and monitoring plan.
  2. Technical approver (service owner) and change board member review within 48 hours.
  3. Schedule into the next change window or approve out-of-window with justification.
  4. Execute, monitor post-change health checks (15/30/60 minutes), and close CR with notes.
- Change Advisory Board (CAB): Weekly CAB reviews for medium/high-risk changes. CAB includes service owners, SRE, Security, and Finance for billing-impacting changes.
- Rollback & post-deploy validation: Every CR must include a rollback plan and explicit success criteria (SLO checks, synthetic tests).
- Emergency changes: Document owner, time of change, immediate mitigation, and schedule a retrospective meeting within 3 business days.

Change windows and blackout periods:
- Regular change windows: Weekdays 02:00–06:00 UTC for low-latency-impact changes, and Saturday/Sunday maintenance windows for larger migrations.
- Blackout periods: High-priority business events (major product launches, end-of-quarter financial close); no non-emergency changes permitted. Calendar of blackout periods is maintained in the company calendar.

3) Data Management
Purpose: Protect data confidentiality, integrity, and availability while balancing developer productivity.
Classification and handling:
- Classification labels: Public, Internal, Confidential, Regulated. Teams must label datasets and store location metadata in the data catalog.
- Storage requirements:
  | Classification | Encryption at rest | Encryption in transit | Retention min | Notes |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|---|
  | Public | Optional | TLS required | 90 days | Suitable for marketing materials |
  | Internal | Required (KMS) | TLS required | 2 years | Internal documentation and telemetry |
  | Confidential | Required (customer KMS) | TLS required | 7 years | PII, customer content |
  | Regulated | Required (HSM/KMS) | TLS enforced with mutual auth | Per contract | Financial/healthcare data |
- Data access requests: Submit request via Data Access Jira form. Approval requires data owner and security sign-off for Confidential/Regulated datasets. Access is time-limited and audited.
- Backups and retention:
  - Daily backups for production data with a minimum 30-day recovery window; longer windows per classification table.
  - Backup verification: monthly restore tests for tier-1 datasets.
- Data deletion: Automated retention jobs and manual deletion requests require evidence of compliance and approval by data owner.
- Data transfers and third parties: All transfers of Confidential/Regulated data require a Data Processing Agreement (DPA) and security questionnaire clearance.

4) Procurement & Expenses
Purpose: Control spend, ensure competitive sourcing, and maintain vendor compliance.
Procurement workflow:
- Small purchases (<= $2,000): Employee submits expense request in expense system; manager approval required.
- Medium purchases ($2,001–$25,000): Procurement request form -> procurement team sources vendors (if applicable) -> manager + finance approval -> PO issued.
- Large purchases (>$25,000): Requires three bids (when practical), procurement lead + finance director approval, legal review for contracts.
- Purchase order (PO) requirements: Cost center, GL code, business justification, expected delivery date, and vendor contact.
- Corporate card policy:
  - Cards issued by Finance based on role.
  - Cards may not be used for contractor payments or recurring vendor purchases that exceed the card limit; such recurring purchases require a PO.
Expense reimbursement:
- Employees must submit itemized receipts within 30 days. Meal per-diem and mileage follow the company rates document. Non-compliant expenses may be denied.

5) Vendor Management
Purpose: Ensure third-party risk is assessed and contractual obligations are tracked.
Vendor onboarding checklist:
1. Procurement submits initial vendor intake form with SOW/scope.
2. Security sends vendor a security questionnaire (standardized) and requests SOC2/ISO evidence if applicable.
3. Legal reviews contract terms, data residency, and indemnities.
4. Finance creates vendor record and configures payment terms.
5. Deliverable acceptance criteria and SLAs are stored in the vendor record.
Ongoing vendor reviews:
- Annual security attestation for vendors with access to confidential data.
- Performance reviews tied to contract milestones.
- Offboarding: revoke all access, ensure final invoices are reconciled, and archive contract documents in the contract repository for the retention period.

6) Travel Policy
Purpose: Clear, fair travel allowances and a streamlined booking & reimbursement process.
Booking and approvals:
- All travel must be booked via the company travel portal (TravelPortal) or via an approved agent.
- Travel requests > $5,000 require VP approval. Managers approve standard travel.
- Preferred suppliers: Finance maintains a list of preferred airlines, hotels, and car services with negotiated rates. Use these suppliers when feasible.
Expenses & reimbursements:
- Per-diem and allowable expenses are documented in the Travel Rates template.
- Employees submit expenses within 10 business days of return with itemized receipts.
- Non-compliant items (e.g., in-room entertainment, minibar) are not reimbursable unless pre-approved.
Safety & emergency procedures:
- Employees traveling to high-risk regions must register with Security and complete a travel risk assessment.
- Emergency contact procedure: notify manager, People Ops, and Security immediately. Company will assist with evacuation where contractually required.

7) Internal Templates & Attachments
- Standard templates (stored in the Templates folder):
  - Purchase Request Template (PR-template.xlsx)
  - Vendor Security Questionnaire (vendor-sq.pdf)
  - Travel Request & Expense Template (travel-expense.xlsx)
  - Change Request Template (CR-template.md)
  - Data Access Request Form (data-access-form.md)
- Template governance: Templates are maintained by the owning team (People Ops, Procurement, Security). Proposed template changes must be submitted as a Git PR against the templates repository and approved by the owning team.

Audit, training, and enforcement:
- Recordkeeping and audits: Each process owner must retain evidence (approval records, receipts, CR tickets) for the configured retention period based on data classification and fiscal policy.
- Training: Mandatory annual training for security, procurement, and expense compliance. New hires must complete policy acknowledgement within their first 7 days.
- Non-compliance: Repeated policy violations will trigger progressive discipline; egregious security breaches will be escalated to Security leadership and People Ops.

Appendices:
A. Approval matrix (summary):
- Expense <= $2,000: Manager
- Expense $2,001–$25,000: Manager + Finance
- Expense > $25,000: Manager + Finance Director + Legal
- Access to Confidential data: Team owner + Security approval

B. Contacts and owners:
- People Ops (policy owner): people-ops@redwood.ai
- Procurement: procurement@redwood.ai
- Security & Compliance: security@redwood.ai
- Finance: finance@redwood.ai

C. Related documents and links:
